claims.claim: Dendrites of consecutively larval-born DL1, DA3, and DC2 adPNs develop in a similar fashion and share a similar targeting region at early pupal stages (0–12 hr APF).
claims.source: In summary, dendrites of consecutively larval-born DL1, DA3, and DC2 adPNs (here collectively named 'early larval-born adPNs'; see its definition in next section) develop in a similar fashion and share a similar targeting region at early pupal stages (0–12 hr APF).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: Early larval-born adPNs segregate into distinct regions close to their adult glomerular positions during mid-pupal stages (21–50 hr APF).
claims.source: This is then followed by their segregation into distinct regions close to their adult glomerular positions during mid-pupal stages (21–50 hr APF).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: From 12 hr to 21 hr APF, DC3/VA1d PN dendrites target the ventrolateral corner of the antennal lobe.
claims.source: We found that, from 12 hr to 21 hr APF, DC3/VA1d PN dendrites targeted the ventrolateral (VL) corner of the antennal lobe (Figure 3C1–4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C1-4.

claims.claim: Early (DL1/DA3/DC2) and mid-early (DC3/VA1d) larval-born adPN dendrites occupy distinct regions at 12 hr APF.
claims.source: Thus, early (DL1/DA3/DC2) and mid-early (DC3/VA1d) larval-born adPN dendrites occupy distinct regions at 12 hr APF.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observations that early larval-born adPNs target the dorsolateral corner while mid-early larval-born adPNs target the ventrolateral corner.

claims.claim: At 12 hr APF, first-born DL1 adPNs send dendrites to the dorsolateral corner of the antennal lobe.
claims.source: Clonal analysis revealed that, at 12 hr APF, the first-born DL1 adPNs sent dendrites to the dorsolateral corner of the antennal lobe as expected (Figure 3D1–3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3D1-3.

claims.claim: At 12 hr APF, dendrites of mid-late larval-born adPNs occupy a large region on the medial/dorsomedial side.
claims.source: By contrast, dendrites of mid-late larval-born adPNs occupied a large region on the medial/dorsomedial (M/DM) side (Figure 3D4—6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3D4-6.

claims.claim: Late larval-born adPN dendrites target the peripheral, dorsomedial corner where N-Cadherin staining is relatively weak.
claims.source: Intriguingly, late larval-born adPN dendrites targeted the peripheral, dorsomedial (abbreviated as pDM) corner where the staining of the pan-neuropil marker N-Cadherin was relatively weak (Figure 3D7–9).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3D7-9.

claims.claim: Larval-born adPNs with adjacent birth order send dendrites to similar regions of the developing antennal lobe.
claims.source: Together, our data (Figure 3A–D) suggest that larval-born adPNs with adjacent birth order send dendrites to similar regions of the developing antennal lobe whereas those with distant birth order send dendrites to distinct regions (Figure 3E2,3).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: Larval-born adPNs with distant birth order send dendrites to distinct regions of the developing antennal lobe.
claims.source: Together, our data (Figure 3A–D) suggest that larval-born adPNs with adjacent birth order send dendrites to similar regions of the developing antennal lobe whereas those with distant birth order send dendrites to distinct regions (Figure 3E2,3).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: The birth order of larval-born adPNs correlates with dendrite targeting in an organized manner (rotating clockwise in the right hemisphere when viewed from the front).
claims.source: Notably, the birth order of the examined PNs does not specify dendrite targeting randomly (Figure 3E4). Rather, the stereotyped dendritic pattern in the prototypic map correlates with the birth order in an organized manner (rotating clockwise in the right hemisphere when viewed from the front; anti-clockwise in the left: early↔DL; mid-early↔VL; mid-late↔M/DM; late↔pDM).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: At 0 hr APF, DL1 PN dendrites are more elaborate than mid-late born PN dendrites.
claims.source: Quantitative analyses of the exploring volume of dendrites and the number of terminal branches showed that, at 0 hr APF, DL1 PN dendrites were more elaborate than mid-late born PN dendrites (Figure 3—figure supplement 3F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3F.

claims.claim: By 6 hr APF, mid-late born adPN dendrites show an extent of innervation comparable to DL1 PNs.
claims.source: By 6 hr APF, the mid-late born appeared to catch up, showing an extent of innervation comparable to DL1 PNs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the quantitative analyses mentioned in the preceding sentence.

claims.claim: Early larval-born adPNs (DL1, DA3, DC2) concentrate their dendrites to the dorsolateral corner by 6 hr APF.
claims.source: We found that whereas early larval-born adPNs (DL1, DA3, DC2) concentrated their dendrites to the dorsolateral corner by 6 hr APF (Figure 3B2; Figure 3—figure supplement 3A5–8), later-born PNs concentrated their dendrites to the medial/dorsomedial or peripheral dorsomedial side at 12 hr APF (Figure 3D4-9; Figure 3—figure supplement 3B5-8, C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3B2 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3A5-8.

claims.claim: Later-born adPNs concentrate their dendrites to the medial/dorsomedial or peripheral dorsomedial side at 12 hr APF.
claims.source: We found that whereas early larval-born adPNs (DL1, DA3, DC2) concentrated their dendrites to the dorsolateral corner by 6 hr APF (Figure 3B2; Figure 3—figure supplement 3A5–8), later-born PNs concentrated their dendrites to the medial/dorsomedial or peripheral dorsomedial side at 12 hr APF (Figure 3D4-9; Figure 3—figure supplement 3B5-8, C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3D4-9 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B5-8, C.

claims.claim: Larval-born adPN dendrites innervate and pattern the antennal lobe using a 'first born, first developed' strategy.
claims.source: Thus, our results suggest larval-born adPN dendrites innervate and pattern the antennal lobe using a 'first born, first developed' strategy.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations that earlier-born PNs develop and target their dendrites earlier than later-born PNs.

claims.claim: Dendritic growth of DA1/DL3 lPNs is evident by the wandering third instar larval stage.
claims.source: Examination of pupal brains double-labeled with DA1/DL3 lPNs (referred to as 'middle larval-born lPNs') and DL1/DA3 adPNs revealed that, like the early larval-born adPNs, dendritic growth of DA1/DL3 lPNs was evident by the wandering third instar larval stage (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: From 0 hr to 12 hr APF, DA1/DL3 lPN dendrites primarily target an area ventrolateral to those of DL1/DA3 adPNs.
claims.source: From 0 hr to 12 hr APF, despite a high degree of overlap among those dendrites that explored the surroundings, DA1/DL3 lPN dendrites primarily targeted an area ventrolateral to those of DL1/DA3 adPNs (Figure 4A1–3; see 3D rendering in Figure 4—video 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4A1-3 and Figure 4—video 1.

claims.claim: At least some adPNs and lPNs sort their dendrites into distinct regions very early on regardless of birth timing.
claims.source: Such a spatial distinction was also observed between middle larval-born adPNs and lPNs in 0 hr and 6 hr APF pupal brains where occasionally single-cell clones from both lineages were simultaneously generated by MARCM (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D1–4, 7–10). Thus, at least some adPNs and lPNs sort their dendrites into distinct regions very early on regardless of birth timing.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3D1-4, 7-10.

claims.claim: Dendrites of early-born lPNs primarily occupy the medial/dorsomedial side of the antennal lobe at 12 hr APF.
claims.source: We found that dendrites of early-born lPNs primarily occupied the medial/dorsomedial side of the antennal lobe (Figure 4B1–3); we note that adPNs born at the same time sent dendrites to the dorsolateral side (see yellow arrowhead in Figure 4B3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4B1-3.

claims.claim: Late-born lPNs send dendrites to the dorsomedial corner.
claims.source: Also, in contrast to the ventrolateral targeting of middle-born lPN dendrites, late-born lPNs sent dendrites to the dorsomedial corner (Figures 4B4—6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4B4-6.

claims.claim: Late-born lPNs innervate the antennal lobe later than earlier-born lPNs.
claims.source: Like larval-born adPNs, late-born lPNs innervated the antennal lobe later than earlier-born lPNs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D7–12–E, G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3D7-12-E, G.

claims.claim: lPN dendrites pattern the developing antennal lobe following similar rules as larval-born adPNs: adjacent birth order → similar dendrite targeting; distant birth order → distinct dendrite targeting; 'first born, first developed.'
claims.source: These data suggest that, at early pupal stages, lPN dendrites pattern the developing antennal lobe following similar rules as larval-born adPNs: adjacent birth order → similar dendrite targeting; distant birth order → distinct dendrite targeting; 'first born, first developed.'
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: The lPN dendritic map formation appears binary: early↔M/DM; middle↔VL; late↔DM.
claims.source: However, unlike the correlation of birth order and target positions in a rotational manner for adPNs (Figure 3E), the lPN dendritic map formation appears binary: early↔M/DM; middle↔VL; late↔DM (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: At 12 hr APF, lPN dendrites mostly occupy the opposite corners along the dorsomedial-ventrolateral axis, leaving the middle of the axis largely devoid of lPN dendrites.
claims.source: Our type-specific characterization corroborated with the gross examination of the lPN dendrites as previously reported (Jefferis et al., 2004): at 12 hr APF, lPN dendrites mostly occupied the opposite corners along the dorsomedial-ventrolateral axis, leaving the middle of the axis largely devoid of lPN dendrites (arrowheads in Figure 1D3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description, a citation to Jefferis et al., 2004, and reference to Figure 1D3.

claims.claim: Lineage and birth order of larval-born PNs contribute to their dendrite targeting in a combinatorial fashion.
claims.source: In summary, we propose that lineage and birth order of larval-born PNs contribute to their dendrite targeting in a combinatorial fashion (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding sections.

claims.claim: The wiring logic of PN dendrites in the developing antennal lobe can be represented by [lineage, birth order]=dendrite targeting.
claims.source: The wiring logic of PN dendrites in the developing antennal lobe can, therefore, be represented by [lineage, birth order]=dendrite targeting; one can deduce the unknown if the other two are known.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding sections.

claims.claim: During normal development, the morphology of the brain lobes changes from spherical at 0 hr APF to more elongated rectangular shapes at 15 hr APF.
claims.source: First, during normal development, the morphology of the brain lobes changes from spherical at 0 hr APF to more elongated rectangular shapes at 15 hr APF (Rabinovich et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rabinovich et al., 2015.

claims.claim: After 22 hr ex vivo culture, the spherical hemispheres of brains dissected at 3 hr APF become more elongated, mimicking ~15 hr APF in vivo brains.
claims.source: After 22 hr ex vivo culture, the spherical hemispheres of brains dissected at 3 hr APF became more elongated, mimicking ~15 hr APF in vivo brains characterized by the separation of the optic lobes from the central brain (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5D.

claims.claim: lPNs in 3 hr APF brains initially produce dynamic but transient dendritic protrusions in many directions, followed by extensive innervation into the antennal lobe.
claims.source: Second, dual-color, two-photon imaging of PNs every 20 min for 22 hr revealed that lPNs in 3 hr APF brains initially produced dynamic but transient dendritic protrusions in many directions, followed by extensive innervation into the antennal lobe (arrowheads in Figure 5E1–3; Figure 5—video 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5E1-3 and Figure 5—video 1.

claims.claim: lPN axons show direction-specific outgrowth of collateral branches into the mushroom body calyx as well as forward extension into the lateral horn.
claims.source: In higher brain centers, lPN axons clearly showed direction-specific outgrowth of collateral branches into the mushroom body calyx as well as forward extension into the lateral horn (arrows in Figure 5E3), thus resembling in vivo development (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5E3 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Larval-specific dendrites observed in 0 hr APF brains cultured for 12 hr ex vivo are no longer seen in those cultured for 24 hr ex vivo.
claims.source: Third, larval-specific dendrites observed in 0 hr APF brains cultured for 12 hr ex vivo (orange arrowhead in Figure 5F4) were no longer seen in those cultured for 24 hr ex vivo (Figure 5F5), indicative of successful pruning and clearance of larval-specific dendrites.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5F4-5.

claims.claim: The size of the developing antennal lobe in brains cultured for 24 hr ex vivo increases considerably.
claims.source: Also, the size of the developing antennal lobe in the brains cultured for 24 hr ex vivo increased considerably (Figure 5F5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5F5.

claims.claim: Olfactory circuit remodeling proceeds normally in the explant system, albeit at a slower rate.
claims.source: These imply that olfactory circuit remodeling (degeneration of larval-specific processes and growth of adult-specific processes) proceeds normally, albeit at a slower rate (compare with Figure 5F1–3).
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observations that pruning and growth occur in the explant system, but the timeline is extended compared to in vivo development.

claims.claim: Dendrites from genetically identified DL1 and DA1/DL3 PNs target to their stereotyped locations in the antennal lobe in 0 hr APF brains cultured for 24 hr ex vivo.
claims.source: Fourth, dendrites from genetically identified DL1 and DA1/DL3 PNs targeted to their stereotyped locations in the antennal lobe in 0 hr APF brains cultured for 24 hr ex vivo (Figure 5G), mimicking in vivo development (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5G and Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The segregation of dendrites of PNs targeting to neighboring proto-glomeruli can be recapitulated in brains dissected at 24 hr APF and cultured for 8 hr.
claims.source: Finally, the segregation of dendrites of PNs targeting to neighboring proto-glomeruli could be recapitulated in brains dissected at 24 hr APF and cultured for 8 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Figure 5—video 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5—video 2.

claims.claim: DC3/VA1d and DA1 PNs exhibit a 1–2 µm increase in the distance between centers of the two dendritic masses during 8 hr ex vivo culture.
claims.source: Specifically, despite constant dynamic interactions among dendrites that explore the surroundings (arrowheads in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A2–4), DC3/VA1d and DA1 PNs exhibited a 1–2 µm increase in the distance between centers of the two dendritic masses and a substantial decrease in the overlap of their core targeting regions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D.

claims.claim: DC3/VA1d and DA1 PNs exhibit a substantial decrease in the overlap of their core targeting regions during 8 hr ex vivo culture.
claims.source: Specifically, despite constant dynamic interactions among dendrites that explore the surroundings (arrowheads in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A2–4), DC3/VA1d and DA1 PNs exhibited a 1–2 µm increase in the distance between centers of the two dendritic masses and a substantial decrease in the overlap of their core targeting regions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D.

claims.claim: DL1 PN dendrites transition from uniform extension in the antennal lobe at 0 hr APF to concentration at the dorsolateral corner at 6 hr APF.
claims.source: Our observation in fixed brains revealed that dendrites of DL1 adPNs transition from a uniform extension in the antennal lobe at 0 hr APF to concentration at the dorsolateral corner of the antennal lobe at 6 hr APF (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of observations from fixed tissue analysis described earlier.

claims.claim: DL1 PNs begin to generate long, albeit transient, dendritic protrusions in the dorsolateral direction at 2 hr 20 min ex vivo.
claims.source: The first sign of active targeting emerged at 2 hr 20 min ex vivo when DL1 PN began to generate long, albeit transient, dendritic protrusions in the dorsolateral direction; these selective protrusions were more prominent at 3 hr ex vivo (arrowheads in Figure 6A4–6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 6A4-6.

claims.claim: During the initial phase of DL1 PN dendrite development, the percentage of dendritic volume in each direction varies from 10% to 40%.
claims.source: During the initial phase, the percentage of dendritic volume in each direction varied from 10% to 40% (Figure 6C and D), indicative of active exploration with little targeting specificity.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 6C and D.

claims.claim: The total amount of DL1 PN dendritic mass in the VM direction over the entire imaging time is the smallest across all samples examined.
claims.source: Despite these variations, the total amount of dendritic mass seen in the VM direction over the entire imaging time (area under the graph of Figure 6C) was the smallest across all samples examined (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 6C and Figure 6E.

claims.claim: The initial phase of DL1 PN dendrite exploration in every direction is followed by a ~4 hr transitional phase during which DL1 PNs predominantly extend dendrites in 2 of the 4 directions.
claims.source: The initial phase of exploration in every direction was followed by a ~4 hr transitional phase during which DL1 PNs predominantly extended dendrites in 2 of the 4 directions (Figure 6C; Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D-E.

claims.claim: During the transitional phase, one of the 2 directions DL1 PNs extend dendrites is always DL whereas the other is either DM or VL but never VM.
claims.source: One of the 2 directions was always DL whereas the other was either DM or VL but never VM.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the time-lapse imaging data.

claims.claim: In the final phase of DL1 PN dendrite development, DL1 PN dendrites always prefer DL out of the two available directions.
claims.source: In the final phase, DL1 PN dendrites always preferred DL out of the two available directions.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the time-lapse imaging data.

claims.claim: DL1 PN dendrite targeting specificity increases over time via active targeting in a specific direction and stepwise elimination of unfavorable trajectory choices.
claims.source: Hence, long-term two-photon imaging of single-cell DL1 PNs revealed that dendrite targeting specificity increases over time via active targeting in a specific direction and stepwise elimination of unfavorable trajectory choices (see summary in Figure 7F1–3).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations from two-photon imaging.

claims.claim: At 3 hr APF, DL1 PNs constantly produce, eliminate, extend, and retract dendritic branches.
claims.source: Quantitative analyses revealed that at 3 hr APF, DL1 PNs constantly produced, eliminated, extended, and retracted dendritic branches (Figure 7A, Figure 7D1, Figure 7—video 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7A, Figure 7D1, and Figure 7—video 1.

claims.claim: At 3 hr APF, stable branches of DL1 PNs spend comparable amounts of time extending and retracting at ~1.5 μm/min.
claims.source: Even stable branches were not immobile. Rather, they spent comparable amounts of time extending and retracting at ~1.5 μm/min (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A1, 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1A1, 1B.

claims.claim: At 3 hr APF, the number of stable branches in the VM direction is significantly lower than in other directions across all 3 hr DL1 PN samples examined.
claims.source: Although there was no correlation between targeting direction and frequency/speed of extension/retraction, the number of stable branches in the VM direction was significantly lower than in other directions across all 3 hr DL1 PN samples examined (Figure 7E1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7E1.

claims.claim: Dendritic branches in the VM direction are short-lived and might be eliminated by retraction.
claims.source: This suggests that even though dendritic branches were developed in every direction at the early stages, those branches in the VM direction were short-lived and might be eliminated by retraction.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that stable branches in the VM direction are less abundant.

claims.claim: From 6 hr to 12 hr APF, DL1 PNs no longer manifest direction-specific branch de/stabilization.
claims.source: From 6 hr to 12 hr APF, DL1 PNs no longer manifested direction-specific branch de/stabilization (Figure 7B–C, Figure 7D2–3, Figure 7—videos 2–3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7B-C, Figure 7D2-3, and Figure 7—videos 2-3.

claims.claim: At 12 hr APF, the abundance of stable branches of DL1 PNs is the highest.
claims.source: At 12 hr APF, the abundance of stable branches of DL1 PNs was the highest (Figure 7D–E1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7D-E1.

claims.claim: The stable branches of 12 hr APF DL1 PNs move at a significantly lower speed (~1 μm/min) than those at 3 hr and 6 hr.
claims.source: Also, the stable branches of 12 hr APF DL1 PNs moved at a significantly lower speed (~1 μm/min) (Figure 7E2) and spent more time being stationary than those at 3 hr and 6 hr (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7E2 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B-D.

claims.claim: Dendritic arborization is evident in terminal branches of 12 hr APF DL1 PNs.
claims.source: Despite the slowdown, dendritic arborization was evident in terminal branches of 12 hr APF DL1 PNs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E), suggesting that PN dendrites are transitioning from simple to complex branch architectures.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: PNs selectively stabilize branches in the direction towards the target and destabilize those in the opposite direction.
claims.source: In summary, AO-LLSM imaging reveals that PNs selectively stabilize branches in the direction towards the target and destabilize those in the opposite direction, providing a cellular basis of dendrite targeting specificity.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations from AO-LLSM imaging.

claims.claim: Upon arrival at the target, dendrite targeting specificity is sustained through branch stabilization in a direction-independent manner.
claims.source: Upon arrival at the target, the specificity is sustained through branch stabilization in a direction-independent manner (summarized in Figure 7F4–7).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations from AO-LLSM imaging.

claims.claim: Embryonic-born PNs prune their larval-specific dendrites during early metamorphosis.
claims.source: Our previous study demonstrates that embryonic-born PNs prune their larval-specific dendrites during early metamorphosis (Marin et al., 2005; Figure 1D1—3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Marin et al., 2005 and reference to Figure 1D1-3.

claims.claim: By 12 hr APF, lov+ PNs already send adult-specific dendrites to a region ventromedial to DC2 PN dendrites.
claims.source: We found that, by 12 hr APF, lov+ PNs already sent adult-specific dendrites to a region ventromedial to DC2 PN dendrites (green arrowhead in Figure 8A3; see 3D rendering in Figure 8—video 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 8A3 and Figure 8—video 1.

claims.claim: lov+ PNs have already caught up with DC2 PNs on dendrite development at 12 hr APF.
claims.source: This implies that lov+ PNs have already caught up with DC2 PNs on dendrite development at this stage, and the re-extension of lov+ PN dendrites must have happened even earlier.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that lov+ PNs have extensive dendrites at 12 hr APF.

claims.claim: lov+ PN dendrites innervate the developing antennal lobe extensively at 6 hr APF.
claims.source: Indeed, we observed lov+ PN dendrites innervated the developing antennal lobe extensively at 6 hr APF (Figure 8A2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 8A2.

claims.claim: lov+ PNs produce nascent branches from the main process dorsal to larval-specific dendrites as early as 3 hr APF.
claims.source: We found that lov+ PNs produced nascent branches from the main process dorsal to larval-specific dendrites as early as 3 hr APF (Figure 8C2–3; arrowheads in Figure 8C6–7).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 8C2-3 and Figure 8C6-7.

claims.claim: lov+ PNs re-extend their adult-specific dendrites at a more dorsal location before the larval-specific dendrites are completely pruned.
claims.source: These data indicate that lov+ PNs re-extend their adult-specific dendrites at a more dorsal location before the larval-specific dendrites are completely pruned.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that nascent adult-specific dendrites appear while larval-specific dendrites are still present.

claims.claim: Multiple embryonic-born PN types already re-extend dendrites to varying extents prior to the separation of larval-specific dendrites from the rest of the processes.
claims.source: Tracing of individual dendritic branches showed that all these PNs already re-extended dendrites to varying extents prior to the separation of larval-specific dendrites from the rest of the processes (Figure 8—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: Concurrent pruning and re-extension apply to multiple embryonic-born PN types.
claims.source: Thus, concurrent pruning and re-extension apply to multiple embryonic-born PN types.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that multiple PN types show simultaneous pruning and re-extension.

claims.claim: Re-extension of embryonic-born PN dendrites occurs in the presumed developing antennal lobe located dorsal to larval-specific dendrites.
claims.source: From 4 hr ex vivo onwards, re-extension occurred in the presumed developing antennal lobe located dorsal to larval-specific dendrites (arrowheads in Figure 8D4–8; see traces in Figure 8D9).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 8D4-8 and Figure 8D9.

claims.claim: Fragmentation of larval-specific dendrites occurs at the distal ends.
claims.source: Live imaging of Split7+ PNs also revealed that fragmentation of larval-specific dendrites occurred at the distal ends (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B1–5), and the process leading to larval-specific dendrites gradually disappeared as pruning approached completion (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B6–10).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 3B1-5.

claims.claim: Pruning of embryonic-born PN dendrites is not initiated by severing at the proximal end.
claims.source: These observations suggest that pruning of embryonic-born PN dendrites is not initiated by severing at the proximal end.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that fragmentation occurs at distal ends.

claims.claim: Dendritic pruning of embryonic-born PNs requires ecdysone signaling in a cell-autonomous manner.
claims.source: It has been shown that dendritic pruning of embryonic-born PNs requires ecdysone signaling in a cell-autonomous manner (Marin et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Marin et al., 2005.

claims.claim: Inhibition of ecdysone signaling by EcR-DN expression suppresses both pruning and re-extension of embryonic-born PN dendrites.
claims.source: We found that inhibition of ecdysone signaling by EcR-DN expression not only suppressed pruning, but also blocked re-extension.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the experiment expressing EcR-DN.

claims.claim: Embryonic-born PNs prune and re-extend dendrites simultaneously at spatially distinct regions.
claims.source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that embryonic-born PNs prune and re-extend dendrites simultaneously at spatially distinct regions, and that both processes require ecdysone signaling (Figure 8E).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement based on the observations described in the preceding paragraphs.

claims.claim: Simultaneous pruning and re-extension explains how embryonic-born PNs can re-integrate into the adult olfactory circuit and engage in its prototypic map formation in a timely manner.
claims.source: Such a 'multi-tasking' ability explains how embryonic-born PNs can re-integrate into the adult olfactory circuit and engage in its prototypic map formation in a timely manner.

results.result: The Drosophila olfactory system serves as a conserved model for studying neural circuit wiring mechanisms. The antennal lobe is functionally equivalent to the vertebrate olfactory bulb, and molecules/mechanisms identified in Drosophila have been shown to play similar roles in mammalian brain wiring.
results.evaluation: C1 establishes the anatomical equivalence between Drosophila and vertebrate olfactory systems based on established knowledge. C2 is supported by three independent citations demonstrating conservation of wiring mechanisms across species. These claims provide appropriate context for the model system.

results.result: PN dendritic patterning creates a prototypic olfactory map prior to ORN axon innervation, demonstrating PN-autonomous targeting ability. PNs are derived from anterodorsal and lateral lineages with invariant birth order, but previous studies could only follow development of a single PN type (DL1).
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C6 are well-supported by multiple prior studies (Jefferis et al., 2001-2004; Marin et al., 2005; Yu et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2012) establishing the developmental timeline and PN-autonomous nature of initial map formation. C7 appropriately identifies the limitation that motivated the current study. These claims establish the foundation and rationale for the work.

results.result: The adult-specific antennal lobe develops alongside degeneration of the larval-specific antennal lobe during early metamorphosis. The developing antennal lobe grows from 0-12 hr APF as PN dendrites innervate it, with PNs sorting dendrites into specific regions by 12 hr APF to form a prototypic map, followed by gradual segregation into non-overlapping glomeruli by 50 hr APF.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C14 are supported by imaging data in Figure 1D1-5 showing the spatial and temporal progression of antennal lobe development. The observations are consistent with prior work (C8-C9 citing Marin et al., 2005) and provide appropriate developmental context. Sample sizes are provided for each timepoint.

results.result: The authors generated new genetic tools using CRISPR/Cas9 to insert T2A-QF2 immediately before stop codons of endogenous genes (CG14322, lov, tsh), creating knock-in driver lines that express QF2 in the same pattern as endogenous genes. These QF2 lines operate orthogonally to GAL4/UAS systems, enabling simultaneous labeling of distinct PN types.
results.evaluation: C16-C17 are supported by transcriptomic data (Figure 2A-B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1-2) and molecular biology methods. C18 is supported by citation to Diao and White, 2012. C19 is supported by citations to Potter et al., 2010 and Riabinina et al., 2015. The genetic strategy is well-documented and builds on established methods.

results.result: DL1 PN dendrites show robust growth by the wandering third instar larval stage, extend radially across the developing antennal lobe at 0 hr APF, concentrate at the dorsolateral corner by 6 hr APF, maintain this position as the antennal lobe grows, and undergo progressive refinement from 21-50 hr APF to form a compact posterior glomerulus.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C24 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3A1-6 with appropriate sample sizes (N=4-14 per timepoint). C20 is additionally supported by citation to Jefferis et al., 2004. The temporal progression is well-documented and provides a baseline for comparison with other PN types.

results.result: Early larval-born adPNs (DL1, DA3, DC2) develop similarly and share targeting to the dorsolateral corner from 0-12 hr APF, with substantial dendritic overlap. Beginning at 21 hr APF, these PNs segregate along medial-lateral and anterior-posterior axes, eventually forming distinct glomeruli separated by intermediate glomeruli by 50 hr APF.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C32 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3B1-6 comparing DL1/DA3 and DC2 PN development with appropriate sample sizes (N=2-12 per timepoint). C27 and C33-C34 are reasonable inferences from the temporal progression observed. The data demonstrate that PNs with adjacent birth order initially target similar regions before segregating.

results.result: Larval-born adPNs with adjacent birth order send dendrites to similar regions while those with distant birth order target distinct regions. The birth order correlates with dendrite targeting in an organized, rotating manner (clockwise in right hemisphere): early→DL; mid-early→VL; mid-late→M/DM; late→pDM.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C39 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3C1-4 and Figure 3D1-9 using both genetic drivers and MARCM clones with appropriate sample sizes. C40-C42 are reasonable inferences summarizing the spatial organization pattern. The rotating pattern represents a novel finding about the logic of initial map formation.

results.result: Larval-born adPN dendrites innervate and pattern the antennal lobe using a 'first born, first developed' strategy. At 0 hr APF, DL1 PN dendrites are more elaborate than mid-late born PNs, but by 6 hr APF mid-late born PNs catch up. Early-born adPNs concentrate dendrites by 6 hr APF while later-born PNs concentrate dendrites by 12 hr APF.
results.evaluation: C43 is supported by quantitative analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 3F. C44-C46 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3B2, Figure 3D4-9, and supplementary figures with appropriate sample sizes. C47 is a reasonable inference from the temporal progression data. The 'first born, first developed' principle is well-supported.

results.result: lPN dendrites pattern the developing antennal lobe following similar developmental rules as adPNs (adjacent birth order→similar targeting; distant birth order→distinct targeting; 'first born, first developed'), but with a binary rather than rotating pattern: early→M/DM; middle→VL; late→DM. Lineage and birth order contribute combinatorially to dendrite targeting, represented as [lineage, birth order]=dendrite targeting.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C53 are supported by imaging data in Figure 4A1-3, Figure 4B1-6, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3D with appropriate sample sizes. C54-C55 are reasonable inferences from the data. C56 corroborates with prior work (Jefferis et al., 2004). C57-C58 represent the key conceptual framework synthesizing the findings. The combinatorial logic is well-supported by the systematic characterization.

results.result: An early pupal brain explant culture system recapitulates key features of in vivo olfactory circuit development, including brain morphology changes, dynamic dendritic protrusions followed by extensive innervation, direction-specific axon outgrowth, pruning of larval-specific dendrites, antennal lobe growth, stereotyped dendrite targeting, and segregation of neighboring proto-glomeruli.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C69 are supported by multiple lines of evidence: C59 by citation to Rabinovich et al., 2015; C60-C69 by imaging data in Figure 5D-G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 with appropriate sample sizes. The explant system validation is thorough, demonstrating that key developmental events occur ex vivo, albeit at a slower rate (C65). This establishes the foundation for subsequent time-lapse imaging experiments.

results.result: Two-photon time-lapse imaging of single DL1 PNs reveals that dendrite targeting specificity increases over time through active targeting in specific directions and stepwise elimination of unfavorable trajectories. DL1 PNs progress through initial (exploration in all directions), transitional (~4 hr, predominantly 2 of 4 directions with DL always included but never VM), and final (preference for DL) phases.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C76 are supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 6A-G with quantitative analysis of dendritic volume in different directions over time (N=3 samples). C77 is a reasonable inference summarizing the mechanism. The stepwise elimination process and directional selectivity are clearly demonstrated, though the sample size is modest (N=3).

results.result: AO-LLSM imaging reveals that PNs achieve dendrite targeting specificity through direction-dependent branch stabilization on the timescale of seconds. At 3 hr APF, DL1 PNs constantly produce, eliminate, extend, and retract branches at ~1.5 μm/min, with significantly fewer stable branches in the VM direction. By 12 hr APF, direction-specific de/stabilization ceases, stable branch abundance peaks, branch speed decreases to ~1 μm/min, and dendritic arborization increases.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C85 are supported by AO-LLSM imaging data in Figure 7A-E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1 with quantitative analysis of branch dynamics (N=3-4 samples per timepoint). Statistical significance is shown for key comparisons (C80, C84). C86-C87 are reasonable inferences from the data. The high temporal resolution (30 sec intervals) provides unprecedented insight into branch dynamics, though sample sizes are modest.

results.result: Embryonic-born PNs re-extend adult-specific dendrites as early as 3 hr APF, before larval-specific dendrites are completely pruned. By 6 hr APF, lov+ PNs show extensive dendritic innervation, and by 12 hr APF they have caught up with larval-born DC2 PNs in development. Re-extension occurs dorsal to larval-specific dendrites, and fragmentation occurs at distal ends rather than by proximal severing.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C98 are supported by imaging data in Figure 8A-D and Figure 8—figure supplement 2-3 with appropriate sample sizes (N=3-12 per timepoint). C88 cites prior work (Marin et al., 2005). C90, C93, C95, and C98 are reasonable inferences from the observations. The data demonstrate simultaneous pruning and re-extension at spatially distinct locations, representing a novel remodeling mechanism.

results.result: Both dendritic pruning and re-extension of embryonic-born PNs require ecdysone signaling in a cell-autonomous manner. Inhibition of ecdysone signaling by EcR-DN expression suppresses both processes. Simultaneous pruning and re-extension at spatially distinct regions explains how embryonic-born PNs can timely re-integrate into the adult olfactory circuit and engage in prototypic map formation.
results.evaluation: C99 is supported by citation to Marin et al., 2005. C100 is supported by experimental data in Figure 8—figure supplement 4 showing that EcR-DN blocks both pruning and re-extension (N≥3 per stage per genotype). C101-C102 are reasonable inferences from the combined observations. The dual requirement for ecdysone signaling in both processes is clearly demonstrated, though the authors note they cannot distinguish whether re-extension failure is secondary to pruning defects.

results.result: PNs use lineage and birth order combinatorially to build the initial dendritic map, with birth order directing dendrite targeting in rotating and binary manners for anterodorsal and lateral lineages, respectively. PN dendrites initiate active targeting with direction-dependent branch stabilization on the timescale of seconds. PNs used in both larval and adult circuits prune and re-extend dendrites simultaneously to facilitate timely map organization.
results.evaluation: These abstract claims (C103-C106) are high-level summaries of the major findings supported by the detailed results described in previous claim groups. C103-C104 summarize the wiring logic findings (supported by claims C40-C42, C54-C58). C105 summarizes the cellular mechanism findings (supported by claims C77, C86-C87). C106 summarizes the remodeling findings (supported by claims C93-C95, C101-C102). All are well-supported by the data presented.
